processing: Made as Taiwanese high mountain oolongs usually are: light oxidation, ball-rolling and little or no roast.
harvest_season: As in the wider Lishan area, typically spring and winter, with fewer pickings than at lower altitudes because of the cold.
appearance_dry: Tight dark-green rolled balls, typical of high mountain oolong.
appearance_wet: Thick, supple green leaves that open fully, as is usual for high-altitude oolong.
taste_profile: Little is recorded specifically for Huagang; expect what is typical of Lishan oolong, with clean floral notes, a thick texture and a cool, sweet finish.

brewing.notes: Typical gongfu settings for a rolled high mountain oolong. Rolled leaf opens slowly, so the first steep runs longest.

vintage_note: As with other Taiwanese high mountain oolongs, it is sold by season and year, usually spring or winter of the current year, and is best drunk fresh. The place name also appears in brand and factory names, so check that the seller means tea grown in the area.
description:
Huagang is one of the named mountain areas of Taiwanese high mountain oolong, listed alongside Lishan, Dayuling and Fushoushan. It lies in the Lishan district of Heping, Taichung, one of the highest tea areas on the island.

Little is documented about Huagang tea on its own. What can be said comes from its class: lightly oxidised, ball-rolled, barely roasted, grown in the cold where leaves develop slowly.

In the cup, typical Lishan oolong is clean, floral and thick-textured, with a cooling sweetness. Use very hot water and allow time for the leaves to open.

The name carries a premium, and sellers do not always use it precisely. A factory or brand called Huagang is not proof of origin, so ask about the garden, the season and the altitude.
history: Huagang is recorded as a named high mountain oolong area, within the Lishan tea district along the Central Cross-Island Highway. The Lishan district is described as lying at about 2,450 m in its highest parts. When tea growing began in Huagang itself, and who pioneered it, is not well documented.
